claims.text: Severe plastic deformation followed by annealing improves the mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy relative to the as-cast alloy.
The material before processing is as-cast FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
The severe-plastic-deformation and annealing treatment is performed at room temperature and atmospheric pressure.
Severe plastic deformation followed by annealing refines the grains of FeNiCrMn alloy.
Severe plastic deformation followed by annealing causes precipitation of secondary phases in FeNiCrMn alloy.
The processing route produces an enhanced dislocation density.
Grain refinement strengthens the alloy through grain-boundary strengthening.
Enhanced dislocation density and grain-boundary strengthening improve the yield strength of FeNiCrMn alloy.
Enhanced dislocation density and grain-boundary strengthening improve the ductility of FeNiCrMn alloy.
There are insufficient data on the mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn alloy after severe plastic deformation and annealing.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies annealing, but the only stated temperature is room temperature. Conventional annealing requires an elevated temperature; separate temperature and duration parameters for deformation and annealing are not supplied.
